Stirling at r=√n+s gives density √(2/π)e^(−2s²), and convergence of probability densities in L¹ follows from pointwise convergence and equal masses. This permits uniform tail removal and replacement by the fixed Gaussian on compact intervals even for rapidly oscillating phases. For γ<1 the bounded-shell phase difference tends to zero, γ=1 gives the characteristic function at frequency βk of N(0,1/4), and γ>1 gives zero for k≠0 by integration by parts (phase derivative has size n^((γ−1)/2), derivative of its reciprocal tends to zero). For either sign of k, S_(n+k)−S_n=k n^(γ/2)+O(n^(γ/2−1)), matching the sign of the unitary conjugation for γ≤1. A band with weights tending to zero is compact by truncation; uniform trigonometric approximation and contraction give the general result. In the Hardy Toeplitz quotient the essential data follow from the continuous effective symbol, including negative winding and nonvanishing heat multipliers.
